reviewer_policy: These are model-reviewed comparative claims. They are not human-established alignments.

method.name: manual_comparative_review_v1
method.limitations: The Chinese witness compresses material distributed across two Pāli paragraphs and differs in itinerary, lodging detail, and retinue count. This is a passage correspondence, not verbal identity.

review.notes: Accepted as a strong narrative passage correspondence. Structural compression and substantive recension variants are preserved in the note; no claim of exact wording or archetype identity.

method.name: manual_comparative_review_v1

shared_sequence: express wonder at Buddha's knowledge of dispositions
repeat teacher criticism versus disciple praise

method.limitations: The Chinese witness presents the discussion as one block and compresses wording. Temporal framing also differs in detail.

review.notes: Accepted as a strong passage-level correspondence based on sequence, actors, and distinctive praise/blame contrast.

method.name: manual_comparative_review_v1

shared_sequence: Buddha becomes aware of the monks' discussion
Buddha goes to the assembly hall and asks what they were discussing
monks repeat the same teacher/disciple praise-blame discussion

method.limitations: The Chinese witness explicitly attributes hearing to the purified divine ear, while the Pāli wording here says the Buddha knew the discussion; this is a recension-level difference inside an otherwise clear narrative correspondence.

review.notes: Accepted as a strong narrative passage correspondence with a notable difference in how the Buddha's awareness of the discussion is expressed.

method.name: manual_comparative_review_v1

shared_doctrine: do not become angry when Buddha/Dhamma/Saṅgha are criticized
do not become elated when Buddha/Dhamma/Saṅgha are praised
signals.shared_transition: moves from reactions to praise/blame toward the topic of minor morality

method.limitations: The Chinese block omits or compresses the Pāli question-and-answer and the explicit instructions to refute what is false and acknowledge what is true. It therefore preserves only part of the Pāli passage's articulated sequence.

review.notes: Accepted specifically as partial overlap, not as a full paragraph equivalence.

method.name: manual_comparative_review_v1

shared_sequence: minor morality introduced as what an ordinary person praises
abstention from taking what is not given

method.limitations: The Chinese witness compresses eight Pāli paragraph units into one block and phrases individual virtues differently. The correspondence is sequential and doctrinal-textual, not verbatim.

review.notes: Accepted as a strong sequential passage correspondence covering the opening of the minor-morality section through the speech precepts.
